'''Luis J. Davidson San Juan''' ({{birth date|1921|09|10}} – {{date of death|2011|11|10}}) was a Cuban mathematician, professor and Doctor in Mathematics, known for his contributions to the fields of mathematics and [[pedagogy]]. He is renowned for receiving the [[Paul Erdős Award]] in 1992 by the [[International Commission on Mathematical Instruction]], and for being awarded the distinction of Maestro Founder of Mathematics in Ibero-America by the [[Organization of Ibero-American States|Organization of Ibero-American States for Education, Science and Culture]]. He was the Vice President of the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] Site Committee in 1988. And he is the author of many books, including ''Equations and mathematicians'' (2008), and ''Problems of elementary mathematics'' (1987).<ref name=falk>{{cite web |url = http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmc/obitdavidson.html |title = Luis Davidson San Juan |last = Falk de Losada |first = Maria |authorlink= María Falk de Losada |date = November 2011 |website = The World Federation of National Mathematics Competitions |publisher = Australian Mathematics Trust |accessdate = May 19, 2013 |url-status = dead |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20130428084301/http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmc/obitdavidson.html |archivedate = April 28, 2013 }}</ref><ref name=bellot>{{cite web |url = http://www.oei.es/oim/revistaoim/numero43/NecrologicaDavidson.pdf |title = Prof. Dr. Luis Davidson San Juan (1921-2011) |last = Bellot |first = Francisco |date = November 2011 |website = Organización de Estados Ibero-Americanos para la educación, la ciencia, y la cultura. |accessdate =20 May 2013}}</ref><ref name=wfnmc>{{cite web|url= http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html|title= David Hilbert and Paul Erdös Awards|author= <!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date= |website= The World Federation of National Mathematics Competitions|publisher= Australian Mathematics Trust|accessdate= 19 May 2013|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171231160201/http://www.amt.edu.au/wfnmcaw.html|archive-date= 31 December 2017|url-status= dead}}</ref>

==Life==

Born in [[Havana]], [[Cuba]] on September 10, 1921, he earned the Doctorate in Physics and Mathematical Sciences from the [[Un<includeonly>|</includeonly>iversity of Havana]] in 1944 with the thesis entitled ''Developments on the series of analytic functions''.<ref name=falk/><ref name=bellot/>

From 1945 to 1961 he taught at the Instituto de Segunda Enseñanza in [[Matanzas]], and in 1950 he was part of the delegation that represented Cuba at the International Congress of Mathematicians at Harvard University.<ref name=falk/><ref name=bellot/>

In 1960, he held the position of National Inspector of Mathematics. And starting in 1963, he organized competitions in mathematics for pre-collegiate students throughout Cuba. 

In 1971, he represented Cuba, as Head of the national delegation in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]], and in 1988, while a member of the organization, he became the Vice President for the IMO Site Committee.<ref name=falk/><ref name=bellot/>

In 1990 he participated in the First Congress of The World Federation of National Mathematics Competitions at Waterloo, and in 1992 he was awarded the [[Paul Erdős Award]] from the International Commission of Mathematical Instruction that was held in Québec, Canada.<ref name=falk/><ref name=wfnmc/>

Some of his books that were published in Spanish are ''Contests in mathematics'' (1974), ''Problems in elementary mathematics'' (1987), and ''Equations and mathematicians'' (1988). The latter was part of a series that he planned to write about: a story about mathematicians and the problems they have solved. 

He died on November 10, 2011.<ref name=falk/><ref name=bellot/>
